RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own. It is a procedural weakness — particularly at a public broadcaster, which usually has balanced-panel guidance — and it removes a safeguard. Treat it as context, not your argument.

Your stronger points: you had nearly double his news experience, you were shortlisted, and no written reasons have come after two weeks. Unexplained silence is what tends to raise questions.

So: chase the written explanation in writing, ask what criteria were weighted and how "digital media" was scored against your experience. Mention panel composition as a process concern. If the reasons never arrive, or shift, the inference strengthens — then consider formal advice.
